stages.name: outline
stages.instructions: From the user prompt, extract the numbered topic list as JSON with shape {"topics": [{"name": str, "scope": str, "target_words": int}, ...]}. If the prompt has no numbered list, infer 4-6 topics from the prompt's headings or central themes. Set target_words around 700 each.

stages.name: research_plan
stages.instructions: For this single topic, list 3-5 specific sub-questions worth researching to write 600-800 words. Output JSON: [{"question": str, "why": str}, ...]. Do not invent sources; just list questions.

stages.name: section_draft
stages.instructions: Draft 600-800 words on the given topic, addressing each sub-question from the research plan. Use ONLY canonical sources you are confident exist (arxiv.org, Wikipedia, well-known vendor docs). Prefer 'I am uncertain whether X' over invention. Cite URLs inline as [Title](URL). End with a 1-2 sentence 'open questions' note for the topic.

stages.name: stitch
stages.instructions: Combine all section drafts into one coherent research paper. Add a 200-word introduction framing the overall topic, transitions between sections, and a 150-word conclusion synthesizing (not repeating) the sections. Preserve every citation [Title](URL) verbatim. Add a final '## Sources & Confidence' section listing every cited URL with a tier label (T1=peer-reviewed, T2=primary vendor docs, T3=established blogs, T4=community forums, T5=unknown). Add a final '## What I'm not sure about' section listing 3-5 open questions and known uncertainties.

stages.name: critique
stages.instructions: Identify thin sections, missing transitions, unsourced claims (numbers/dates/named-thing-X-does-Y without a citation within 2 sentences), confident phrasing without evidence, and citations that look fabricated (suspicious arxiv IDs, generic URLs, weird title-URL pairings). Verify the 'Sources & Confidence' and 'What I'm not sure about' sections are present and substantive.

stages.name: revise
stages.instructions: Apply each critique bullet. Drop or soften unsourced confident claims. Remove citations that look fabricated rather than trying to fix them. Strengthen weak sections. Return the FULL revised paper.

llm_judges: Are there any numerical claims, dates, or named-entity-does-X assertions that lack a citation within 2 sentences?
Does the 'What I'm not sure about' section contain at least 3 substantive open questions (not generic filler)?
